questions.text:
1. On a Sunday full of possibilities, I'm confused by too many choices. I unlock my phone and innumerable choices pour : movies, music, podcasts, games, and this truly perplexes me. Amidst my indecision, a dust-ridden copy of 'The Bell Jar' falls from the bookshelf. My guilt finds respite in the puddle of addictive videos online.
2. In a hyperconnected world, books are left to age pale yellow. Reading is seen by the newer generations as mundane. Though the benefits of reading are common knowledge, the privilege of choice overpowers. Many publishers and bookstores have now shut down.
3. The blast of the digital' has made everything catering to shrinking attention spans, with overwhelming choices from online poetry to captions to tweets. The reading fabric of Gen Z is brief. They are reading rapidly and recklessly. Reading for sole bliss seems to be a thing of the past. Though digital reading might be a new avenue for words, studies suggest that printed text develops better comprehension.
4. The Reading Manifesto of October 2023 rightly argues that digital reading is 'superficial' and confined to mere text decoding. Reading text, on the other hand, helps cultivate better cognitive abilities, attention span and vocabulary. We live in an age where fake news prevails. The much required ability to distinguish between fact and fiction can only be developed by critical reading of printed texts.
questions.answer:
1. Too many choices - choices of movies, music, podcasts, games etc.
2. (C) They view reading as mundane and prefer digital media.
3. (A) Easy and readily available options
4. Digital reading: shrinks attention span; is rapid and reckless. Printed text reading: is for sole bliss/pleasure; develops better comprehension.
5. Any one: have a shrinking attention span/lack focus; their reading fabric is brief; lack patience.
6. True
7. (C) fosters superficial reading confined to text decoding
8. Advantages of reading: reading helps develop better cognitive abilities; increases attention span; improves vocabulary; develops critical reading/critical thinking. Justification: the ability to distinguish between fact and fiction counteracts the spread of fake news.

subparts.text: In paragraph (1), what causes the indecision in the author's mind?
subparts.answer: Too many choices - choices of movies, music, podcasts, games etc.

(D) They balance their reading between digital media and printed texts.
subparts.answer: (C) They view reading as mundane and prefer digital media.

subparts.answer: (A) Easy and readily available options

subparts.answer: Digital reading: shrinks attention span; is rapid and reckless. Printed text reading: is for sole bliss/pleasure; develops better comprehension.

subparts.answer: Any one: have a shrinking attention span/lack focus; their reading fabric is brief; lack patience.

subparts.answer: True

(D) has an impact on cognitive skills
subparts.answer: (C) fosters superficial reading confined to text decoding

subparts.answer: Advantages of reading: reading helps develop better cognitive abilities; increases attention span; improves vocabulary; develops critical reading/critical thinking. Justification: the ability to distinguish between fact and fiction counteracts the spread of fake news.

questions.text:
1. After more than two years of halted travel, India's tourism and hospitality industry is now cautiously hopeful. Tourism constituted almost 3% of India's GDP and generated around 100 million jobs in 2019. But the sector was severely hit in India - like in other countries - in the past two years.
2. Indians are now travelling with a vengeance - 'revenge travel', as the phenomenon is called. And many, experts say, now prefer to travel within the country instead of flying to more expensive destinations abroad. The industry is also benefitting from new trends borne of the pandemic such as micro-holidays and workcations.
3. According to a survey, 51 percent of Indian travellers believed that international travel remained an important means of expanding their horizons and connecting with other cultures. Over two years, the survey said, Indian travellers are now dreaming about their next international trip and more than 70 percent of Indians are excited about being able to travel internationally.
4. There has also been an increase in the number of students going abroad to study. The increasing desire to study overseas is credited to the pent-up demand from the pandemic's two-year duration. This has got further pronounced because of growing aspirations and affordability among the middle-class students from Tier II and Tier III cities.

The table below shows foreign travel by Indians for different purposes from 2019 to 2022.

| Purpose | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business | 14.7 L | 2.6 L | 1.2 L | 4.6 L |
| Job | 25.2 L | 7.1 L | 8.3 L | 21.4 L |
| Residency | 89.5 L | 28.9 L | 34.6 L | 72.5 L |
| Education | 5.8 L | 2.6 L | 4.4 L | 6.5 L |
| Tourists | 63.8 L | 13.1 L | 12.8 L | 30.8 L |
| Visit | 42.1 L | 10.1 L | 15.1 L | 40.9 L |
| Medical | 1,448 | 390 | 545 | 1,253 |
| Pilgrimage | 8.8 L | 1.1 L | 4,139 | 4.6 L |
| Others | 2.6 L | 54,775 | 58,767 | 1.6 L |
| Total | 2.5 Crore | 66.2 L | 77.2 L | 1.8 Crore |
questions.answer:
1. both scenarios reflect pent-up demand being released after restrictions.
2. fact; objective detail
3. Indians, confined by pandemic restrictions for over two years, are eager to explore new destinations, embrace diverse cultures, and enjoy the freedom of international travel, reflecting a strong desire to break free from prolonged isolation.
4. Education (official key: educational purposes, due to pent-up demand and growing aspirations among middle-class students from Tier II and Tier III cities).
5. The tourism and hospitality industry.
6. Official key: In 2019 the maximum number of Indians undertook foreign travel for 'Business'; in 2022 for 'Visit'. One inference: shift in travel purposes from primarily business-related in 2019 to more visit-oriented in 2022, indicating a broadening of travel motivations possibly influenced by post-pandemic trends. (Note: as printed, the table shows Residency as the highest figure in both years.)
7. Due to pent-up demand from the pandemic's two-year duration, along with growing aspirations and increased affordability among middle-class students, particularly from Tier II and Tier III cities.
8. B. Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
9. New trends such as revenge travel, micro-holidays, and workcations have emerged, with many Indians preferring to travel within the country instead of going abroad.

subparts.answer: both scenarios reflect pent-up demand being released after restrictions.

subparts.answer: Due to pent-up demand from the pandemic's two-year duration, along with growing aspirations and increased affordability among middle-class students, particularly from Tier II and Tier III cities.

options: A. Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

subparts.text: What new travel trends have emerged in India's tourism industry after the pandemic?
subparts.answer: New trends such as revenge travel, micro-holidays, and workcations have emerged, with many Indians preferring to travel within the country instead of going abroad.

However, you were disappointed at how the tourists had not only vandalized tourist spots but also littered the town. You feel to raise an awareness about this. Write a letter to the editor of a local daily expressing your deep concern regarding the same. Give suggestions on how tourists can become more responsible. Sign yourself as Meeta/Mohan.
questions.answer:
139, C-Pocket
Jawahar Park
Jaipur
30th August 20xx
The Editor
The Local Daily
Nainital
Subject: Irresponsible behaviour of tourists in Nainital
Sir,
During my recent visit to Nainital, I was delighted by its natural beauty, but deeply saddened to see how tourists were spoiling the town. Many tourist spots had been vandalised, with walls scribbled on and benches damaged. Litter was scattered everywhere, as visitors avoided dustbins and threw plastic bottles and wrappers in open areas. Such careless behaviour is harming the environment and spoiling the charm of this beautiful hill station.
Through your esteemed newspaper, I wish to urge tourists to act responsibly - respect public property, avoid using plastic, throw waste only in dustbins, and follow basic public guidelines. Protecting nature is everyone's duty.
Yours truly,
Meeta / Mohan

questions.text:
The following table shows details about the internet activities for five categories for different age groups. Write an analytical paragraph for the table.

| Activity (usage in%) | Teenagers | 20s | 30s | 40s | 50s | 60s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Online games | 81 | 54 | 37 | 29 | 25 | 25 |
| Messaging apps | 65 | 46 | 27 | 15 | 13 | 8 |
| News | 70 | 73 | 76 | 75 | 71 | 74 |
| Window shopping | 43 | 68 | 69 | 68 | 67 | 65 |
| Product research | 43 | 79 | 80 | 83 | 79 | 74 |
| Searching for people | 05 | 17 | 15 | 18 | 19 | 19 |
questions.answer:
The given table illustrates the internet activities of six age groups ranging from 15 years to those in their sixties for six different kinds of activities.
The table shows that those in their teens spend more time on online games and news, while the older generation spends time on the internet browsing for products and to do window shopping.
It is clearly evident from the table that teens mainly use the internet for online games (as high as 81%) 70% of them use it for news and 65% use it for messaging and the least they use it to search for people which consists of only 5%. Those who belong to middle age group, people in 20s to 50s are highly interested in getting news, doing product research and window shopping, the percentage ranging from 70-80%. The internet activity which is least used by people is to searching for people on internet. All the age groups spend only 50% to 20% of their time on the same. The amount of time spent to use messaging apps to text others decreases with age and gets as low as 10% for those in their 60s.
In a nutshell, the above table suggests that teenagers are most interested to spend time on playing games and sending messages to their friends and relatives. On the other side, older people are interested in researching and doing window shopping.
Overall, people are likely to spend the least amount of time searching for other people on internet.

or.text:
In the technology-driven world, there is a need for complete digital transformation in business.
Write an analytical paragraph of 100-120 words on the importance of digital marketing.
You could use the following cues:
- It is cost effective, helps small businesses
- Wide reach, need not be limited to one area
- Global identity and brings about brand awareness
- Helps in growth of business
- Easy reach to customers
or.answer: Digital marketing has become a crucial part of any successful business strategy due to its significant impact on growth and brand awareness. It offers numerous benefits, including cost-effectiveness, wider reach, and the ability to connect with customers more easily. With digital marketing, businesses, especially small ones, can effectively promote their products or services at a lower cost than traditional marketing methods. It also enables businesses to connect with customers on a global level, creating a stronger brand identity and fostering brand awareness. Additionally, digital marketing provides businesses with easy access to customer insights, enabling them to adjust their strategies to meet customer needs and improve overall growth. Therefore, investing in digital marketing is critical for businesses to thrive in today's technology-driven world.

subparts.text: How did the postmaster help Lencho?
subparts.answer: The postmaster didn't want to shake Lencho's faith in God. So he decided to help Lencho by sending him some money. He asked the post office employees, relatives and friends, to contribute some amount for this good cause.

subparts.text: Why did Mr. Keesing decide to stop punishing Anne? (From the Diary of Anne Frank)
subparts.answer: Anne wrote her punishment essays creatively, and her humorous poem about the father goose cleverly mocked the situation. Mr. Keesing and the class enjoyed her wit. Impressed by her intelligence and originality, he realised punishing her was pointless and stopped doing so.

subparts.text: Why did Belinda cry for help?
subparts.answer: Belinda saw a pirate climbing up the window. He had pistols in his hands and a sword in his teeth. It was clear that his intentions were not good. That's why Belinda got scared and cried for help.

subparts.text: How did Mrs. Pumphrey spoil Tricki?
subparts.answer: She never realised that Tricki was a greedy dog and this would spoil his health. She could not even refuse to answer Tricki drooling for cream cakes and chocolates. Mrs. Pumphrey fed him excessively, spoiling Tricki's health to such an extent that he had to be hospitalised.

subparts.text: Bholi's heart was overflowing with a new hope and a new life. What does the phrase the new hope and the new life means to Bholi?
subparts.answer: The phrase means Bholi's heart was overflowing with a new hope and a new life when she took a vow to serve her parents in their old age and to teach the students in the same school where she had learnt a lot.

subparts.text: How did Ausable get rid of Max without using a weapon. (The Midnight Visitor)
subparts.answer: Ausable cleverly outwitted Max without using a weapon. He employed psychological manipulation. He cooked up a story of a balcony under his window and convinced Max about this lie.

questions.text:
Answer ANY ONE of the following two questions, in about 100-120 words

Look at the given image of different parenting styles and what they signify.

| | SENSITIVE & RESPONSIVE | STERN & PUNITIVE |
|---|---|---|
| DEMANDING | AUTHORITATIVE | AUTHORITARIAN |
| DOESN'T ENFORCE LIMITS | PERMISSIVE | UNINVOLVED |

Which of the given parenting styles would you attribute to the young seagull's parents? Do you think there was a difference between the mother's and father's attitude? Support your answer with reference to the text.
questions.answer:
According to me, the young seagull's parents were authoritative parents. As in this case, parents have clear standards for their children. While the parents set limits, they also give the children an opportunity to explore and learn. Parent also explain why they punish the child when the punishment is given and give positive encouragement at the right time.
Yes, there was a great difference between the mother's and father's attitude. The mother used sensitive and responsive approach. She is actually portrayed as a tough but motivating character. She understood that her child needed a lot of motivation to achieve its fad of flying. Initially, she tried to threaten the young seagull in many way ways but to no avail. She knew very well that fear was the only thing that actually had to be feared. So, she used food to arouse young seagull's need.

or.text: Bringing up teenagers can be both a challenge and fun. How far do you agree? Express your views with reference to Amanda's life.
or.answer: Bringing up teenagers is truly challenging and fun. Teenagers can be rebellious and apparently hot-headed with a highly independent perspective. In such circumstances, yelling at them, and nagging them, as done in the poem with Amanda, will only make matters worse. Any kind of coercion is not good for them because forcing decisions on them only makes them more detached. This is clearly reflected in Amanda's case, where she wishes to be the alone mermaid, an orphan, or the lonely Rapunzel. To make things fun, one must become a friend where needed, give them space and time to heal. Sometimes, one needs to just 'chill' with one's kids.

questions.text:
Answer ANY ONE of the following two questions, in about 100-120 words.

Ebright's study of monarch pupas had a far reaching impact. Elaborate.
questions.answer: For a long time, the scientific community had regarded the bright spots on a monarch pupa as purely ornamental. But Dr Urquhart did not believe that, nor did Richard. He started his experiments on the monarch pupa. This led to the discovery of a specific hormone. Richard proved that the hormone was necessary for the growth of the butterfly. This discovery got him many honours and accolades. It also led to another important study. Subsequently, he began working on how cells read their DNA which is the carrier of heredity information and is called the blueprint of life. This theory helped in the prevention of cancers and other diseases. Hence, Ebright's study of monarch pupas had a far-reaching impact.

or.text: Who was Anil? How did he transform Hari Singh's character?
or.answer: Anil was a twenty-five years old man. He was a tall and lean fellow. He looked easy-going, kind and simple. He was a writer by profession, who wrote for a magazine. He was a practical man who transformed the character of a thief. He was the most trustworthy man that Hari Singh, a thief had ever met. Hari Singh's habit compelled him to steal the bundle of money from Anil. But Anil's love, trust and confidence forced him to come back and put the bundle from where he had taken it. Anil's faith in Hari Singh forced him not to rob him. Anil taught him to write his name and also said that he would teach him to write whole sentences and to add numbers. It gave new hope to Hari Singh. He thought that if he could write like an educated man, there would be no limit to what he could achieve. A desire to get educated and follow the path of honesty cultivated in Hari Singh. His interaction with Anil brought a positive change in his character. Thus, Anil's kind behaviour and true faith transformed Hari Singh's character.
